tool_input.description: Probe whether Builder.get() replaces deprecated build()

result:
`./compile.sh` reports success.

I created `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class for the package-private `org.apache.commons.csv.Lexer`. Notes on approach:

- `Lexer`, `CSVFormat`, `ExtendedBufferedReader`, and `Token` are all in the same package but only `Lexer`'s javadoc was provided; the others (needed to build fixtures) aren't documented. I used the long-stable, well-known Apache Commons CSV public API (`CSVFormat.DEFAULT`, `CSVFormat.Builder`) and the package-private `ExtendedBufferedReader`/`Token` shapes, then let the compiler itself validate every assumption (e.g. it revealed `Builder.build()` is deprecated in favor of `Builder.get()`, which I adopted).
- Tests cover every method in the javadoc: `close`/`isClosed`, `getBytesRead`/`getCharacterPosition`/`getCurrentLineNumber`, `getFirstEol`, `isEndOfFile`, `isStartOfLine` (including the "start of file" sentinel via `ExtendedBufferedReader.getLastChar()`), `isQuoteChar`, `isCommentStart`, `isEscape`, `isDelimiter` (including multi-char delimiter peek non-consumption), `isEscapeDelimiter` (using the exact example from the javadoc), `readEndOfLine` (CR/LF/CRLF boundary cases), `readEscape` (EOF-after-escape error case plus literal-character happy paths), `trimTrailingSpaces`, and `nextToken` (simple records, no-trailing-newline boundary, quoted fields, comments, surrounding-space trimming, empty-line skipping, and token-instance reuse).
- No other files were modified; no tests were run, only compiled per the restrictions.
